title: Post-failover validation and routing swap checklist
summary: Living draft: pragmatic checklist and verification steps to run immediately after failing over a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) and when swapping network routing. Includes Terraform notes and quick rollback triggers.
body:
Purpose:
This is a practical, checklist-style runbook for operators and SREs to validate system integrity and customer connectivity after a failover or when performing a routing weight swap for private deployments (VPC or on-prem). It intentionally focuses on fast, observable checks that catch silent data divergence, secret/credential mismatch, and routing misconfigurations.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to private deployments managed by Redwood Private where traffic may be redirected between primary and standby sites, or between old and new cluster deployments.
- Assumes Terraform-managed infra and that there is a working state backend with locking (S3+Dynamo/consul).
- Assumes SNAT/egress, KMS, and DB credentials have been synced via vault or equivalent prior to swap.
- This is NOT a full restore playbook; it focuses on validation, routing swap, and rollback triggers.

Quick rules of engagement:
- Owner for the swap: Ops on-call + Eng PM notified.
- Cutover window: keep DNS TTL low (<= 60s) and use LB weight shifts where possible.
- If ANY critical validation fails, rollback immediately to previous routing weights and file an incident.

Prereqs before any routing swap:
- Confirm terraform state lock: terraform plan succeeds and no pending apply (terraform plan -lock-timeout=30s).
- Database replication lag < 3s (pg_stat_replication lag < 3 seconds) or within SLA for the customer.
- KMS/HSM keys active and accessible: key_status check in vault and cloud logs.
- Secrets sync: vault kv get for service accounts used by runtime nodes.
- KV cache snapshot present (if used): latest-kv-checksum recorded in S3.
- Smoke test harness (local) available and mapped to target endpoint.

Pre-swap verification checklist (run sequentially):
1) State and diffs
   - terraform state pull > /tmp/state.json && git diff -- /tmp/state.json against expected workspace snapshot.
   - Verify no unexpected provider versions or module sha mismatches.
2) Storage & backups
   - S3 snapshot present for last known-good time: aws s3 ls s3://redwood-private-backups/<cluster>/YYYYMMDD
   - Run sha256sum on latest snapshot metadata and compare to recorded manifest.
3) DB consistency
   - Check replication health: SELECT now()-pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp() AS replay_lag;
   - Run small row-count checks on critical tables (jobs, model_metadata) across primary/standby.
4) Secrets & certs
   - vault status && vault kv get -format=json secret/private/<deploy>/service-account > /dev/null
   - Verify TLS cert expiry for fronted hostnames (openssl s_client -connect host:443 -servername host).
5) Runtime readiness
   - Node agent heartbeat count >= expected (kubectl get pods -l app=runtime -n redwood | grep Running | wc -l).
   - Check model weights loaded: curl -s http://<node>/internal/metrics | grep model:loaded | sort -u
6) Telemetry sanity
   - Recent traces exist for heartbeats and token consumption in the last 5 minutes.
   - Alerts: ensure no new SEV0/SEV1 alerts in prometheus for the target cluster.

Traffic cutover plan (safe progressive method):
- Phase 0: Dry-run - validate health checks and run smoke tests against the target with a small internal header (x-internal: dry-run). Do not change routing.
- Phase 1: 5% weight to target LB, monitor 10 minutes for errors and latency p50/p95.
- Phase 2: 25% weight for 10–15 minutes, run full end-to-end smoke tests (auth, inference, embeddings, streaming).
- Phase 3: 60% weight for 10 minutes with increased load tests (simulate normal traffic).
- Phase 4: 100% if all metrics within thresholds.
- Each phase: wait at least two aggregation windows (our default Metric window=60s) before proceeding.

Cutover metrics to watch (must be green to proceed):
- 5xx rate: target <= baseline + 0.1%
- Latency p95: target <= baseline * 1.25
- Token throughput: within -10% of baseline
- Error types: no new authentication failures, no model-load errors, no missing kv-cache hits spike

Post-swap validation (immediate checks):
- Run the smoke suite end-to-end (auth -> request -> token accounting -> billing tag) against production customer-facing route.
- Confirm token accounting sequence IDs increment and match the expected sequence (sample logs and check last 100 IDs).
- Check billing metadata tags present on outgoing usage events.
- Run consumer-facing health checks (simulate 3 customers of varying sizes).
- Reconcile top 10 customers' tail latencies and error rates against pre-cutover snapshot.
- Verify model outputs for a seeded set of prompts (stored in /playbooks/validation-prompts). Compare exactness/semantic similarity; flag any drift > threshold.

Terraform module and state notes (practical tips):
- Use workspace-specific state files for each deployment: terraform workspace select <deploy>-staging/production.
- Always run terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan and inspect plan for resource replacements that may cause IP changes (LB, NAT).
- When upgrading module versions that touch networking: run a canary apply in a staging copy of the same VPC (copy state or use a transient workspace) and test routing swap there first.
- State drift: if terraform state shows replaced instances, consider resource targeting (terraform apply -target=module.runtime) and use blue/green for nodes to avoid wholesale replacement.
- Locking: ensure DynamoDB lock TTL > expected apply time or use manual lock if the apply will be long.

Upgrade plan considerations (minor vs major):
- Minor (patch): can be applied during traffic shift windows; use small canary and increase weights.
- Minor (module-only): prefer in-place rolling updates, ensure new module does not change IPs or LB names.
- Major (networking or DB changes): requires full maintenance window; ensure rollback artifacts available: DB basebackup, snapshot checksum, terraform state snapshot.

Rollback triggers (immediate rollback if any occur):
- 5xx spike > 0.5% absolute increase for > 3 minutes
- Data divergence detected by table row-count diff > 1% for critical tables
- KMS/HSM access errors for any runtime node
- Token-accounting mismatch or negative balances observed

Rollback steps (fast path):
1) Set LB weights back to previous values (recorded prior to cut).
2) If DNS was changed, revert DNS record and increase TTL to normal afterwards.
3) Re-run smoke tests against the previous routing; confirm baseline restored.
4) Open incident with linked artifacts and attach logs collected during the failure window.

Quick command snippets (copy-paste):
- Lock/inspect state:
  terraform workspace show && terraform state pull | jq '.modules | length'
- Snapshot manifest checksum:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-private-backups/<cluster>/manifest.json - | jq -r '.sha256'
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-private-backups/<cluster>/snap-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz - | sha256sum -c -
- PG replication lag:
  psql -c "SELECT now()-pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp() as lag;" -h standby-host -U repl_check
- Curl model load metrics:
  curl -s http://<node>:9090/metrics | grep 'model_load_success' || true

Post-event collection checklist (after the swap or rollback):
- Collect system metrics (prometheus export tarball) and save to s3://redwood-private-archives/incidents/<incident-id>/metrics.tar.gz
- Export logs (k8s + runtime) covering -10 to +30 minutes around swap and upload to secure bucket.
- Export terraform state snapshot and store alongside incident artifacts.
- Fill incident template: summary, timeline, root cause hypotheses, action items with owners.

Runbook maintenance notes (how to keep this doc fresh):
- Run a table-top drill with SRE, Solutions Eng, and Customer Success every quarter for one representative customer.
- After each drill, update the validation prompts and the failure thresholds in the checklist.
- Link new Terraform module PRs that modify networking to this doc (see linked_artifacts).

Open questions and flagged items (TODOs):
- Add automated checksum verification step to the restore pipeline (owner: Priya).
- Create a small synthetic workload runner that can operate at 5% of traffic and run during Phase 1 (owner: Noah).
- Formalize token-accounting smoke tests to be part of CI for private deploys (owner: Liam).

Notes to self / operator reminders:
- Always record pre-swap weights and current terraform workspace name in the incident channel before proceeding.
- If a long-running terraform apply is needed, consider manually rotating nodes instead of full replacement.
- Symmetric testing: after reaching 100% on target, run a reverse traffic test (shift 10% back to source for 10 minutes) to validate bi-directional parity.

References and helpful links:
- Private deploy runbooks (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Private+Deploy+Runbooks
- Terraform modules repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/412
- Recent related incident: JIRA INF-987
